the tracking algorithms can be categorized into four types, and the best-performing algorithms are the combination of the best-performing approaches of each type.

The main takeaway from our work is that

there is no single tracking algorithm that performs best in all situations, and thus, it would be desirable for the tracking community to develop a tracking toolbox that can be used as a plug-and-play module for various applications.

the tracking performance is highly dependent on the initial conditions and the algorithm design, and it is important for researchers to carefully consider the evaluation criteria and the initialization conditions when evaluating their proposed methods.
a large-scale benchmark dataset and an open code library are essential to advance the state-of-the- art in the field.
